boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented St. Mary’s traditions and tradition-linked landmarks, from orientation rituals to the campus Seven Wonders.

cards.title: Church Point, a Seven Wonders landmark
cards.subtitle: Seven Wonders of St. Mary’s tradition
cards.notes: Visit the waterfront landmark in daylight and use the College’s Seven Wonders page to place it in the campus tradition.
cards.short_summary: A historic point recognized among the College’s Seven Wonders.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies Church Point as one of its Seven Wonders, important landmarks linked to student traditions.
cards.source_title: The Seven Wonders of St. Mary’s
cards.access_notes: Use established campus paths and follow posted waterfront guidance.

cards.title: Find the Hidden Grave
cards.subtitle: First-year Seven Wonders tradition
cards.notes: Treat the search as a history prompt: locate only publicly accessible cemetery markers and leave the site exactly as found.
cards.short_summary: A Seven Wonders mystery associated with first-year students.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says the Hidden Grave is meant to be found by first-year students and notes student-newspaper evidence from 1959.
cards.source_title: The Seven Wonders of St. Mary’s
cards.access_notes: Respect cemetery grounds, markers, and any access restrictions.

cards.title: Pause at the Garden of Remembrance
cards.subtitle: Seven Wonders of St. Mary’s tradition
cards.notes: Use this Seven Wonders stop for a quiet look toward the St. Mary’s River; keep the visit low-impact and respectful.
cards.short_summary: A 1934 garden recognized in the College’s Seven Wonders.
cards.evidence_claim: The College lists the Garden of Remembrance among the Seven Wonders and says it was built and dedicated in 1934.
cards.source_title: The Seven Wonders of St. Mary’s
cards.access_notes: Follow campus access rules and preserve the garden setting.

cards.title: See the Freedom of Conscience Statue
cards.subtitle: Seven Wonders of St. Mary’s tradition
cards.notes: Photograph the state-commissioned landmark from a lawful public viewpoint and read its College history; do not alter or climb it.
cards.short_summary: A campus icon whose history includes documented student lore.
cards.evidence_claim: The College lists the Freedom of Conscience Statue as a Seven Wonder and documents historical student pranks connected to the campus icon.
cards.source_title: The Seven Wonders of St. Mary’s
cards.access_notes: View only from lawful public areas; do not touch, climb, or modify the statue.

cards.title: Start at the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Seven Wonders student-use tradition
cards.notes: See the Bell Tower as part of the Seven Wonders route and, if a course is set up, follow all recreation and facility rules.
cards.short_summary: A memorial tower that became a Frisbee-golf starting point and hole.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says student use began soon after the Bell Tower was built, as the starting point for Frisbee golf tournaments, and that it remains a golf hole.
cards.source_title: The Seven Wonders of St. Mary’s
cards.access_notes: Do not climb the tower; observe posted recreation and memorial-site rules.

cards.title: Spot the Shoe Tree legacy
cards.subtitle: Seven Wonders graduation tradition
cards.notes: View the tree between Prince George and Dorchester halls and use the College history to understand its graduation connection.
cards.short_summary: A shoe-covered campus landmark tied to graduating seniors.
cards.evidence_claim: The College dates the Shoe Tree tradition to about 1983–86 and says it began as a living legacy for seniors to throw in shoes upon graduation.
cards.source_title: The Seven Wonders of St. Mary’s
cards.access_notes: Look and photograph from the ground; do not throw objects or damage the tree.

cards.title: Great Bamboo Boat Race
cards.subtitle: Hawktoberfest tradition at the River Center
cards.notes: Register for Hawktoberfest and watch teams build with provided bamboo before racing; racers should follow the event’s current rules.
cards.short_summary: Teams construct bamboo boats and race them at the College’s fall gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM calls the Great Bamboo Boat Race a time-honored St. Mary’s College tradition and describes teams crafting boats from bamboo and provided materials.
cards.access_notes: The cited event required preregistration to race; confirm current Hawktoberfest details before attending.

cards.title: Sign the President’s Book
cards.subtitle: New-student matriculation tradition
cards.notes: If you are an incoming student, follow orientation instructions for the signing and regard the entry as part of the College record.
cards.short_summary: New students mark matriculation by signing a long-running College book.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM describes new students signing the President’s Book as a tradition dating back several decades and a record of matriculation.
cards.source_title: St. Mary’s College of Maryland Welcomes Students Back to Campus
cards.access_notes: Participation is arranged through new-student orientation; confirm current instructions with Student Affairs.

cards.title: Walk the Sacred Journey
cards.subtitle: Commemorative-to-waterfront observance
cards.notes: When the observance is scheduled, join the respectful procession, listen to the readings, and follow accessibility and parking guidance.
cards.short_summary: An emerging College tradition honoring enslaved people of Southern Maryland.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM calls the Sacred Journey an emerging tradition in which the community walks the path taken by enslaved people who once toiled there.
cards.source_title: The Sacred Journey: The Beloved Community, Nov. 14
cards.access_notes: The cited College event states there is no cost and that the public is welcome; check the next observance for current details.

cards.title: Begin with Hawks in the Community
cards.subtitle: Orientation service and exploration tradition
cards.notes: Incoming students can select an orientation service or exploration activity and use it to learn about Southern Maryland organizations.
cards.short_summary: A reinstated orientation tradition connecting new Seahawks with the region.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM says Hawks in the Community is the reinstatement of a long-standing orientation tradition connecting students with local organizations and businesses.
cards.source_title: New Seahawks Launch College Journey with Day of Service and Exploration
cards.access_notes: Offered through orientation; choose a current approved activity and follow organizer guidance.
